title: Desire and being satisfied
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What do you want so much that its absence makes you unhappy?

I said the third philosopher is famous for saying, as I put it, that people suffer either because their desires are not fulfilled, or from boredom when the desires are satisfied. He believed desire was the cause of misery, and pessimism.
I said I don't think that idea comes from that philosopher. I think it comes from Taoism, which is much older.

I summarized Taoism as four things: embracing the simplicity of life, embracing the primitive things like eating and sleeping, reducing selfishness, and the most important and relevant, not having desire.

You might think that is impossible, I said, and people would argue that it is. Taoism says you shouldn't pursue desire: you should allow things to unfold naturally, because if we desire love in our relationships and don't get it, we get disappointed.
A student said: so it is more like being satisfied in the present. I said: yes, a lot of it is about being satisfied in the present.
Where in your life would you let things unfold?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write one desire you hold that you might drop.
Write the disappointment it has caused.
Write what satisfied in the present would look like for you.
Write one simple thing you could embrace today.
Write who could check my summary of these ideas.

check.q: What did I say Taoism says about desire?
choices: Don't pursue it; let things unfold naturally

check.q: What did a student say Taoism sounds like?
What did I say causes disappointment?
choices: Desiring something and not getting it

recap: Notice the desires that disappoint you. Practise being satisfied in the present.
